This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- from the respondents on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 17-08-2022 at about 9.30 a.m., the petitioner and his friend one Mr. Vijaya Kumar were proceeding on Jupiter Scooter bearing No. KA-02-JH-8193 from 8th Mile on Tumkur- Bengaluru main road (NH-4), towards Goraguntepalya, in front of Rack Line Mal, near Jalahalli Cross Junction, Bengaluru City.
The petitioner was riding the above said motorcycle slowly and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations, on the left side of the said road.

At that time the driver of the Tata Mini Goods vehicle bearing No. KA-52-A-7271 came from back side, in a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, without observing any traffic rules and regulations and dashed to the scooter of petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as Coolie and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Peenya Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.

Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.

It has contended that, the Devendra Reddy vs Sri Sai Krishna Transport Co on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100713211/
2 petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

The investigation officer in his final report has clearly stated that, on the alleged date, time and place of accident, due to rash and negligent driving of the Goods Canter vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-52-A-7271 the said accident has taken place and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of his body.

13. The Ex.P.4 spot mahazer & sketch, clearly speaks that, the accident has taken place on 30 feet width Tumkur- Bengaluru NH-4 road and the petitioner was riding his scooter bearing No.
KA-02-JH-8193 on left side from the center line of the road.

Further it reveals that, the offending Goods Canter vehicle bearing No. KA-52-A-7271 has dashed to the scooter of petitioner from back side and there was sufficient space towards both side of the place of accident, to pass easily and avoid the said accident by the driver of offending vehicle.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.5, the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicles and the accident has taken place due to dashing of offending vehicle from the back side, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing is elicited in the cross- examination of P.W.1, to show

that,
there is no fault or negligence on the part of driver of offending Goods Canter vehicle.
Further, as on the date of accident the driver of offending vehicle was holding a valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle, the place, date and time of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.8 wound certificate, Ex.P.13 and 14 discharge summaries, Ex.P.17 lab reports (total 5), Ex.P.18 consultation records (total 18), Ex.P.19 X-rays (total 10), Ex.P.20 X-ray, Ex.P.21 clinical notes and Ex.P.22 case-sheets, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered right elbow fracture dislocation and right ankle bimalleolar fracture.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not led any evidence to substantiate the contentions taken in its written statement.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Goods Canter vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-52-A-7271 and there is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Goods Canter vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-52-A-7271 and he has sustained right elbow fracture dislocation and right ankle bimalleolar fracture and for the said injuries he has underwent surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life,
loss of prospects of marriage etc.,

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.10.
As per Ex.P.10, the date of birth of the petitioner is 01-07-1956.
The accident has taken place on 17-08-2022 at about 9.30 A.M.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is 66 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined and treated the petitioner has clearly deposed in his examination-in- chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered right elbow fracture dislocation and right ankle bimalleolar fracture.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has 74% physical disability of right arm and for the whole body he has 25% physical disability.
The oral evidence of P.W.2 is fully corroborated with documentary evidence.

The Ex.P.8 wound certificate,
Ex.P.13 and 14 discharge summaries, Ex.P.17 lab reports (total 5), Ex.P.18 consultation records (total 18), Ex.P.19 X-rays (total 10), Ex.P.20 x-ray, Ex.P.21 clinical notes and Ex.P.22 case-sheets clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered right elbow fracture dislocation and right ankle Devendra Reddy vs Sri Sai Krishna Transport Co on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100713211/

sentences.text: Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross- examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the Ex.P.20 to 22 documents are not related to the petitioner, there is no disability to him and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 17-08-2022 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 14-12-2023, which is after lapse of one year and three months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, floating elbow with loosened implants and non union fracture of the medial malleolus with implant in situ.
Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the disability of 20% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified
. Hence, in the instant case the disability of 20% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as coolie and was earning income of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do any work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was doing coolie work.
Therefore, notional income is to be considered as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2022.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.
b)

As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 66 years is 5.

Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,86,000 X 20/100 X 5 = Rs.1,86,000/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.5,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 30 medical bills, as per Ex.P.15.

All the bills have been examined carefully and found that, in bill at Sl.No.1 the grand total is Rs.2,53,181/-, out of the said amount Rs.1,338/-
discount has been given by the hospital authority and Rs.2,00,000/- has been paid by ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company and rest of the amount of Rs.51,843/- only has paid by the petitioner.
But, the petitioner while totaling the bills has calculated Rs.2,51,843/-.

Therefore,
excluding the above excess amount of Rs.2,00,000/- calculated by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,84,238/- towards medical expenses.

7 iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.
suffered right elbow fracture dislocation and right ankle bimalleolar fracture.
As per Ex.P.13 and 14 discharge summaries, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 09 days from 17-08-2022 to 22-08-2022 and 15-09-2022 to 17-09-2022, in Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru.
Further, as per P.W.2 the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:

As per Ex.P.13 and 14 discharge summaries, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 09 days from 17-08-2022 to 22-08-2022 and 15- 09-2022 to 17-09-2022,
in Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 9 = Rs.9,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:

As per Ex.P.13 and 14 discharge summaries, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 09 days from 17-08-2022 to 22-08-2022 and 15- 09-2022 to 17-09-2022,
in Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru.
Therefore, compensation of Rs. 800 x 9 = Rs.7,200/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Sriramanagara, Bengaluru North,
Bengaluru, the accident has taken place at 8th Mile on Tumkur- Bengaluru main road (NH-4),
towards Goraguntepalya, in front of Rack Line Mal, near Jalahalli Cross Junction, Bengaluru City and he has taken treatment at Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between all the above three places, compensation of Rs.2,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 9 days as inpatient at Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.
He might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost his income for the said period.

Therefore, Rs.15,500 x 2 =
Rs.31,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 66 years and unfortunately he has suffered right elbow fracture dislocation and right ankle bimalleolar fracture.
The evidence shows that, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 20% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants which would cost around Rs.60,000/-.
The cost of surgery for radial head replacement quoted by P.W.2 seems exaggerated.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

20. Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Goods Canter vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-52-A-7271 the accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,19,438/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
21. ISSUE No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.5,19,438/- (Rupees five lakhs nineteen thousand four hundred and thirty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Due to said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Peenya Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the Devendra Reddy vs Sri Sai Krishna Transport Co on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100713211/
2 petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
opennyai_summary.issue:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident alleged to have occurred on 17-08-2022 at about 9.30 a.m., Jalahalli Cross Junction, National Highway No.4, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tata Mini Goods Vehicle, bearing registration No.
KA-52-A- 7271 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3
. What order or Award ?
6.
17. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 17-08-2022 at about 9.30 a.m., at 8th Mile on Tumkur-Bengaluru main road (NH-4), towards Goraguntepalya, in front of Rack Line Mal, near Jalahalli Cross Junction, Bengaluru City, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Goods Canter vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-52-A-7271.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
that,
there is no fault or negligence on the part of driver of offending Goods Canter vehicle.
Further, as on the date of accident the driver of offending vehicle was holding a valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle, the place, date and time of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Goods Canter vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-52-A-7271 and there is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
15.
Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a Devendra Reddy vs Sri Sai Krishna Transport Co on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100713211/
5 criminal case are not required."
16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.
If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the disability of 20% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified
. Hence, in the instant case the disability of 20% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do any work.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was doing coolie work.
Therefore, notional income is to be considered as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2022.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.

Therefore,
excluding the above excess amount of Rs.2,00,000/- calculated by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,84,238/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.
19. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1 . Loss of future income Rs. 1,86,000-00 2.
Attendant charges 9,000-00 5.
Conveyance expenses 2,000-00 7. Loss of income during 31,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 40,000-00
9. Future medical expenses 20,000-00 Total Rs. 5,19,438-00
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,19,438/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,19,438/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
21. ISSUE No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.5,19,438/- (Rupees five lakhs nineteen thousand four hundred and thirty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened Devendra Reddy vs Sri Sai Krishna Transport Co on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100713211/
9 on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in his name as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e- payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
